author: val
body: Answering Maybe is what makes the rule stated above this chapter's Encode section true rather than merely written down. Until 2026-07-28 nothing enforced it: a pipe in any of the six free-text header fields shifted every field by one, and sdw-decode answered Just a record in which eight of ten readings were wrong, silently, with only sdw-hash surviving because it precedes the injected pipe. The content field is deliberately not checked, since a pipe is how the language writes a sum type and the length prefix plus take-the-rest is exactly what lets the content hold them. sdw-encode-unchecked is the body, split out so the check is visible at the one place that decides.

author: val
body: Six fields, not nine. sdw-signature is emitted as hex from a byte list and cannot contain a pipe by construction, and sdw-timestamp and the content length are shown from Integers. Checking those three would be checking that show emits digits.

author: blu
body: The ninth pipe ends the header; the content is the next `len` characters, taken whole. A header with fewer than nine fields, or a line with no ninth pipe, is not this format and decodes to None.
